_doc: Generated-only replacement placement spec. Heading anchors were retained from the original reviewed placement file.

figures.alt: White exterior dryer-vent hood with a backdraft flap on a light stucco wall
figures.caption: Trace the dryer route from the appliance to the exterior termination before replacing a vent. Short, direct, supported runs are safer than hidden bends and an exterior hood needs to remain accessible for cleaning.
figures.before: When You Need a Permit in Jacksonville

figures.alt: Attic ventilation housing with a supported duct and clear insulation around it
figures.caption: Remove crushed or disconnected ducting and support the replacement so lint cannot collect in a sag. A dryer duct needs its own appropriate route and should not be confused with a bathroom or attic ventilation path.

figures.alt: Attic insulation held clear of a roof-edge ventilation path
figures.caption: Verify that the dryer exhausts outdoors and does not dump humid air into the attic. Moisture and lint together create a building and fire-safety problem that calls for a corrected route, not a hidden connection.
